title: Reverse Conway's law and GenAI: How agents will take over the organisation - Patrick Debois
talk_summary: A speculative keynote about how GenAI changes organizational structure (Conway's law reversed), moving from copilot to teammate to peer to manager, with commentary on trust, failure handling, and ROI of agents vs humans.

takeaways.technique: Agents as peers with explicit code-of-conduct guardrails
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agents should get explicit rules/guardrails analogous to a human code of conduct, and warns that one misbehaving agent can influence others (toxic agent dynamics), so agent-to-agent influence needs watching like team dynamics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some have started talking about toxic behavior of an agent like one agent is influencing other agents to do bad things

takeaways.technique: ROI-per-agent accounting in the org chart
takeaways.what_they_do: Suggests treating agents as org-chart units with an explicit cost/output ratio (what is one agent worth vs N humans) to drive hiring/planning decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what is the equivalent of one agent is it like five humans what's the cost

takeaways.technique: Build the thing that builds the thing
takeaways.what_they_do: Advises shifting from doing the work to designing/supervising the system that does the work, so you retain enough understanding to supervise and handle failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: stop building the thing like don't build the software yourself but kind of think about like how you would build the thing
